guard: public history abort stops the active JetStream pull and dashboard deadlines pass that abort to every unfinished source
why: FOUR MUTATIONS across the public API, broker pull buffering, newest-N paging, and dashboard threading.
M1 removes the public AbortSignal. The real constrained-link call stays pending and retains its
M2 restores one whole-pending pull. An aborted read then leaves the broker committed to sending
the entire backlog down a connection whose reader has left. What that costs is measured in TOTAL
bytes moved, not in bytes arriving after the abort: the page is committed and delivered before the
reader gets to leave, so 165B arrives after the abort either way. Cell 7.3 discriminates on the
total, which is why the mutation names it.
M3 disables the rolling tail eviction. A widened history window then returns its oldest limit
messages instead of the newest N.
M4 removes the dashboard signal from channel reads. The focused web seam names the missed source.
All anchors are unique code-only spans. Core mutants rebuild before their public entry-point suites.

mutations.name: the multi-filter read stops batching, so one create carries every channel again and a large space gets the timeout that returned no chat at all
mutations.expectRed: 8.0 10000 channel filters ANSWER at all, where one unbatched create timed out
mutations.cell: 8.0 10000 channel filters ANSWER at all, where one unbatched create timed out
mutations.note: One batch holding every subject IS the unbatched create. Measured before the fix on an isolated broker, 10,000 filters failed `timeout` after 5,023ms while 5,000 answered in 5,345ms, and the route then served a page marked partial with `chat` missing and no chat entries. 8.0 asserts messages rather than the partial marker, so it is the cell this mutation reaches first: everything above section 8 reads 69 channels, which is one batch either way.

mutations.name: the batched pages are merged by the payload's ts instead of by stream sequence, so which messages the page holds depends on sender clocks again
mutations.find: const rows = pages.flat().sort((a, b) => a.seq - b.seq).slice(-limit);
mutations.replace: const rows = pages.flat().sort((a, b) => a.msg.ts - b.msg.ts).slice(-limit);
mutations.expectRed: multiChannelHistory merges BATCHES by arrival, not by the highest `ts`
mutations.cell: multiChannelHistory merges BATCHES by arrival, not by the highest `ts`
mutations.note: Repointed after MEASUREMENT. It first named web cell 8.4, which compares a one-create read against a forced-batch read. That cell SURVIVED this mutation, and the reason is structural rather than incidental: the mutation reorders BOTH arms identically, so an equality between two arms of the same implementation cannot see the key it sorts on. The tie-based reasoning offered for it was wrong. The core suite pins the key against an ORACLE instead: a corpus published frame by frame so that `ts` and arrival disagree, where selecting by `ts` returns the other message. 8.4 is kept, because batch-invariance is worth asserting, but it is not this mutation's detector. RE-AIMED after a WRONG-RED: the first name pointed at the single-batch check, which stays GREEN under this mutation because streamHistory applies the limit inside the one batch, leaving one row for the merge to sort. The multi-batch check is the earliest red and is now asserted first, since this suite stops at the first failure.
